title: The 365-Day Chair Yoga & Resistance Band Journey
subtitle: A Full Year of Gentle, Joint-Friendly Movement & Nutrition
welcome: This book is your day-by-day companion for a full year of gentle, chair-based movement. It blends seated chair yoga with light resistance band training and simple, joint-friendly nutrition guidance — designed for anyone who wants to move every day without strain, whether you are managing joint pain, recovering mobility, or simply building a sustainable habit.

Research on chair-based yoga programs consistently links regular practice with better flexibility, improved balance, less joint stiffness, and reduced pain for people with conditions such as osteoarthritis, with benefits that can last for months after a program ends. Even a few sessions a week, done consistently, can make a meaningful difference — and this program gives you a full year of structure so you never have to guess what to do next.
365 days organized into 52 weeks across four progressive phases.
Each day lists a focus, a short warm-up, 3-4 main exercises with reps or hold times, and a cool-down.
A Master Exercise Library (with full cues) is in the next section — the daily calendar refers to exercises by name.
Two days each week use a light-to-medium resistance band; the rest use only a sturdy chair.
One rest day and one active-recovery day are built into every week.
Each week includes one nutrition focus to pair with your movement practice.
safety_first: Check with your doctor or physical therapist before beginning any new exercise program, especially with an existing joint or health condition.
Use a sturdy, armless chair with non-slip feet, placed on a stable surface.
Move within a pain-free range. Mild muscle effort is normal; sharp or joint pain is a signal to stop or modify.
Breathe steadily throughout — never hold your breath during effort.
Stop any exercise that causes dizziness, numbness, or sharp pain, and rest.
Progress at your own pace — the phase intensities are a guide, not a requirement.
daily_warmup: Deep Belly Breathing — 5 breaths, settle in and set an intention
Seated Shoulder Rolls — 10 reps, loosen the upper back
Seated Neck Rolls — 5 each direction, ease tension
Seated Marching — 20 reps, wake up the legs and raise heart rate gently
Seated Torso Circles — 5 each way, mobilize the spine
daily_cooldown: Seated Forward Fold — 5 slow breaths, release the low back
Seated Chest Opener — 30 seconds, counter rounded posture
Guided Seated Meditation — 2-3 minutes, settle the nervous system
Deep Belly Breathing — 10 breaths, close the practice calmly

nutrition_guide.intro: This is general wellness education, not medical advice — check with your doctor or a registered dietitian for guidance specific to any health condition or medication.

sections.heading: Core Principles
items: Hydrate consistently — cartilage and joint tissue depend on water throughout the day.
Favor anti-inflammatory foods: fatty fish, olive oil, colorful vegetables and fruit, nuts, seeds, and whole grains.
Include a protein source at each meal to support muscle maintenance alongside your movement practice.
Limit added sugar, fried foods, and heavily processed snacks, which are linked with more inflammation.
Add warming spices like turmeric, ginger, and cinnamon regularly — long used for their soothing qualities.

sections.heading: A Simple Joint-Friendly Plate
items: Half the plate: colorful vegetables (leafy greens, peppers, broccoli, carrots).
A quarter of the plate: lean protein (fish, poultry, eggs, beans, lentils, tofu).
A quarter of the plate: whole grains or starchy vegetables (quinoa, brown rice, sweet potato).
A thumb of healthy fat: olive oil, avocado, nuts, or seeds.

sections.heading: Sample 7-Day Meal Rhythm
items: Breakfast: overnight oats with berries and flaxseed, or eggs with sautéed greens.
Lunch: big salad with beans or grilled chicken, olive oil dressing, and whole-grain bread.
Dinner: baked salmon or lentil stew with roasted vegetables and a small serving of whole grain.
Snacks: Greek yogurt, a handful of walnuts, fresh fruit, or vegetable sticks with hummus.

reflection_log.intro: Photocopy this page or keep a simple journal. Each week, jot down:
items: How your joints and energy felt this week
Which exercises felt easiest and which felt most challenging
Any changes to sleep, mood, or daily activities
One small nutrition win from the week
